name: Paddle

header.quote: All webhooks sent by Paddle include a `Paddle-Signature` header.

scheme.value: HMAC-SHA256 with the destination's endpoint secret key string used as-is as the key (UTF-8 bytes of the whole string, including its pdl_ prefix; no base64 decoding); h1 is the lowercase hex digest. The prose does not name the encoding; the manual Node example uses .digest('hex') and the manual C# example uses new HMACSHA256(Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(secretKey)).
scheme.short: HMAC-SHA256, hex; the secret string itself is the key

signed_content.value: the ts value, a colon, then the raw request body: ts:body
signed_content.quote: The extracted timestamp (`ts`) + A colon (`:`) + The raw body of the request

header_format.value: semicolon-separated key=value pairs: ts=<unix seconds>;h1=<signature>. Always at least one h1; during secret rotation more than one h1 is returned.

header_parts_quote.value: ts: Unix timestamp. h1: event signature; at least one, more than one during rotation.
header_parts_quote.quote: Signatures contain at least one `h1`. We may add support for secret rotation in the future. During secret rotation, more than one `h1` is returned while secrets are rotated out.

secret_source.value: Dashboard: Paddle > Events > Notifications, edit the destination, copy the secret key field. API: GET /notification-settings/{notification_setting_id} returns endpoint_secret_key (example value looks like pdl_ntfset_..._<random>).
secret_source.quote: Send a GET request to the `/notification-settings/{notification_setting_id}` endpoint. If successful, Paddle returns the notification destination settings, including the `endpoint_secret_key`.

secret_scope.value: per notification destination (so per endpoint; sandbox and live accounts are separate)
secret_scope.quote: Paddle generates a secret key for each notification destination that you create.

timestamp_tolerance.value: Docs recommend checking ts against the current time and rejecting events that are too old. They state the SDK helper default tolerance is five seconds. No tolerance is stated for manual verification beyond 'may like to check' and 'too old'.
timestamp_tolerance.quote: our SDK helper methods check the timestamp (`ts`) against the current time and reject events that are too old. The default tolerance between the timestamp and the current time is five seconds.
timestamp_tolerance.short: Five seconds in Paddle's SDKs; "reject events that are too old"

rotation.value: During rotation Paddle sends more than one h1 in the header. Receivers should accept if any h1 matches (the docs say 'more than one h1 is returned'; they do not spell out the accept-any rule). Wording 'We may add support for secret rotation in the future' suggests the feature is not fully described; grace period length not stated.
rotation.quote: During secret rotation, more than one `h1` is returned while secrets are rotated out.

raw_body_note.value: Do not transform the raw body at all (no whitespace or other formatting changes), or signatures will not match.
raw_body_note.quote: Don't transform or process the raw body of the request, including adding whitespace or applying other formatting.

node.value: await paddle.webhooks.unmarshal(rawRequestBody, secretKey, signature)  (package @paddle/paddle-node-sdk; rawRequestBody is the body as a string, signature is the paddle-signature header; returns the event entity, throws on mismatch)
node.quote: const eventData = await paddle.webhooks.unmarshal( rawRequestBody, secretKey, signature, );

python.value: from paddle_billing.Notifications import Secret, Verifier; integrity_check = Verifier().verify(request, Secret('WEBHOOK_SECRET_KEY'))

dotnet.value: no official .NET SDK helper shown (the SDK tabs cover Go, Node.js, PHP and Python). The docs do give a manual C# example (HMACSHA256 over ts:body, key = UTF-8 bytes of the secret string).

example_header_only.value: The docs print an example Paddle-Signature header but no secret or body, so it is NOT a usable test vector.

method_and_content_type.value: HTTPS POST with a JSON payload. Content-Type header value not stated. User agent string is 'Paddle' (docs advise matching it in firewall rules).
method_and_content_type.quote: Can accept `POST` requests with a JSON payload

event_type_location.value: top-level JSON field event_type, format entity.action (for example customer.created)
event_type_location.quote: `event_type` | The type of event, in the format `entity.action` (for example, `customer.created`).

delivery_id.value: event_id (evt_ prefix) is the dedupe key and is the same across retries and across destinations; notification_id (ntf_ prefix) identifies the delivery to one destination. The page describes notification_id as 'for this delivery attempt' yet also says one notification is retried, so treat event_id as the dedupe key as Paddle instructs.
delivery_id.quote: `event_id` | Unique ID for this event, prefixed with `evt_`. Use this to deduplicate events you may receive more than once.
delivery_id.short: event_id (evt_...), the same on every retry

notification_id_quote.value: notification_id: unique ID prefixed ntf_; a single event can produce multiple notifications (one per destination)
notification_id_quote.quote: Each notification has its own `notification_id` but they share the same `event_id`.

handshake.value: not stated by the provider (no challenge or ping on setup)

batching.value: one event per request: every webhook has the same top-level structure (event_id, event_type, occurred_at, notification_id, data)
batching.quote: Every webhook Paddle sends has the same top-level structure, regardless of the event type

success_status.value: HTTP 200. Any other status code is treated as failure and retried.
success_status.quote: If your server sends another kind of status code or doesn't respond within five seconds, Paddle automatically retries

response_deadline.value: five seconds; respond before doing any internal processing
response_deadline.quote: should respond with an HTTP `200` status code **within five seconds**.

retries.value: Live accounts: up to 60 attempts over about two days (around 10 in the first hour, around 45 in the first day); wait before the next attempt is 60 x n^1.1 seconds where n is attempts made so far (table: attempt 2 after 1m, attempt 3 after 2m 9s, attempt 60 after 1h 28m, 1d 18h since first). Sandbox accounts: 3 attempts in total, within about two minutes (20s, then 43s). Times approximate; an attempt can be up to a minute later.
retries.quote: For sandbox accounts, we make 3 attempts in total, all within about two minutes. For live accounts, we make up to 60 attempts in total over about two days.
retries.short: Live: up to 60 attempts over about two days; sandbox: 3 in about two minutes

disabling.value: not stated by the provider (docs say a notification whose attempts are exhausted gets status failed and can be replayed via the API; they do not describe Paddle deactivating the destination)
disabling.quote: When all attempts to deliver a webhook are exhausted, its status is set to `failed`.

ordering.value: Order not guaranteed; store and check occurred_at before making changes.
ordering.quote: We can't guarantee the order of delivery for webhooks. They may be delivered in a different order to the order they're generated. Store and check the `occurred_at` date against a webhook before making changes.

duplicates.value: At-least-once delivery; make processing idempotent, dedupe on event_id.

events.full_list_index: https://developer.paddle.com/llms/webhooks.txt (each event has its own page under developer.paddle.com/webhooks/<group>/<event>)

common.meaning: a subscription record was created (checkout of a recurring item)
common.quote: Occurs when a subscription is created.
Occurs when a subscription becomes active.

common.meaning: any change to a subscription (items, scheduled change, billing details)
common.quote: Occurs when a subscription is updated.
Occurs when a subscription is canceled.

common.meaning: a renewal transaction is unpaid; status becomes past_due
common.quote: Occurs when a subscription has an unpaid transaction. Its `status` changes to `past_due`.

common.meaning: payment captured; earliest point you can be sure payment succeeded
common.quote: Occurs when a transaction is paid. Its status field changes to `paid`.

common.meaning: Paddle finished all internal processing of the transaction
common.quote: Occurs when a transaction is completed. Its status field changes to `completed`.

common.meaning: a payment attempt on a transaction failed
common.quote: Occurs when a payment fails for a transaction.
Occurs when a customer is created.

common.meaning: a refund, credit or chargeback adjustment was created
common.quote: Occurs when an adjustment is created.

checkout_sequence.value: typical order: transaction.created, customer.created, address.created, business.created (optional), transaction.paid, subscription.created (if recurring), transaction.completed
checkout_sequence.quote: For a subscription, `transaction.paid` is the earliest point at which you can be sure payment has been captured.

where_url_is_entered.value: Dashboard: Paddle > Events > Notifications > New destination (description, type webhook or email, URL, API version, usage type, events); or the create notification setting API. Max 10 active destinations.
where_url_is_entered.quote: You can create as many notification destinations as you want, but only 10 can be active at once.

test_tools.value: Webhook simulator (Paddle > Events > Simulations, or POST /simulations): single events or scenarios; destination usage type (traffic_source) must be 'all' (Platform and simulation) or 'simulation'; platform-only destinations receive real events only. Sandbox accounts also exist. Failed notifications can be replayed through the replay notification API.
test_tools.quote: Only destinations with the **Usage type** (`traffic_source`) of **Platform and simulation** (`all`) or **Simulation** (`simulation`) work with webhook simulator.

ip_allowlist.quote: We recommend adding Paddle webhook IP addresses to your allowlist, and rejecting webhooks that come from other sources.

gotchas.value: Respond 200 before doing any internal processing; queue events and process asynchronously.
gotchas.quote: You should respond before doing any internal processing.

gotchas.value: Serverless cold starts can cause intermittent five-second timeouts; consider pre-warming.
gotchas.quote: consider pre-warming your function to prevent cold starts that might cause intermittent timeouts.

gotchas.value: A WAF may incorrectly block Paddle; bypass bot checks on the webhook path, restrict by Paddle IPs and user agent 'Paddle'.
gotchas.quote: requests from Paddle may be blocked incorrectly.

gotchas.value: Sandbox and live use different IP lists and have different retry schedules (3 attempts vs up to 60).
gotchas.quote: Allow different IP addresses for `sandbox` and `live` accounts:

gotchas.value: Platform-type destinations never receive simulated events.
gotchas.quote: Platform destinations can only receive traffic for real events to avoid sending simulated data to production endpoints.

unreadable.why: 404 in markdown form; the event index was read from developer.paddle.com/llms/webhooks.txt instead; full_list_url points to the working index

research_notes: The manual Ruby example on the signature page rejects events older than 5 seconds (current_time - event_time > 5), consistent with the five-second statement.
The 5 second SDK tolerance appears twice on the signature page (SDK info callout and manual step 2); both say five seconds.
